reviews.title: Best in the market!
reviews.text:
I got the Moto Book 60 for 48k and I have been really happy with it so far. The Bronze Green colour makes it stand out. It looks quite different and premium compared to other laptops in this range.

Performance is solid(Core 5-210H processor). It handles my daily work and multitasking easily. Battery backup is also pretty good for an H-series chip, I usually get around 5 to 5.5 hours, which I wasnt expecting. I am seeing people complaining about the battery backup. It is a H series processor, what did you guys expect?
So, always think about what you need before buying something.

The best part has to be the OLED display with 120Hz. Its super smooth and the colours look amazing; watching videos or just using the laptop feels great. The keyboard is also excellent, similar to what you'd expect from Lenovo, comfortable and responsive for long typing sessions.

There is one solid downside for me is the speaker volume, its a bit on the lower side compared to other laptops i have seen in this category of thin and light laptops. There is also a small nitpick for me, there are no first party apps for this laptop like lenovo vantage and etc. But other than that, it has all the necessary ports and overall feels like a very balanced machine.

Definitely a good choice if you're looking for performance and a great display while being thin and light for portability. I would rate it 4/5.

reviews.text:
The laptop itself offers solid value for money, and the display quality is impressive even at 60 Hz. However, the listing is misleading.
Only the 2.8K OLED variant comes with a 120 Hz refresh rate, while the WUXGA OLED version is capped at 60 Hz. Because both variants are grouped under the exact same listing, the reviews and star ratings are pooled together, which creates unnecessary confusion for buyers expecting 120 Hz across the board.
The seller/brand should separate these into distinct listings so ratings reflect each specific configuration accurately. A good product, but the listing lacks transparency.
